item.title: 68-year-old Sheila Consaul bought Ohio lighthouse for $71,010 in 2011, restored it for over $300K
item.description: At 68, Sheila Consaul owns Ohio’s historic Fairport Harbor West Lighthouse, which she bought for $71,010 at auction in 2011. After years of restoration and more than $300,000 in investment, she transformed the abandoned century-old landmark into an off-grid summer home featuring rainwater collection, solar power, historic interiors and stunning views of Lake Erie. item.title: In 1911, Norwegian whalers released 10 reindeer on South Georgia for food and hunting
item.description: In 1911, reindeer were introduced to South Georgia by Norwegian whalers. This led to significant ecological issues, as the absence of natural predators allowed their numbers to explode, resulting in harm to delicate coastal ecosystems and native species. A comprehensive eradication initiative was launched, successfully culling almost 7,000 reindeer, thereby aiding the natural recuperation of the damaged habitats, with native flora and seabirds starting to reappear. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.description: Val Ripley, aged 101, continues her lifelong fascination with dolls' houses and their historical significance. The collection features dolls' houses dating back to 1840, reflecting evolving domestic life. Val's enduring connection to these tiny worlds spans nearly a century. item.description: Isabella Neff's generous donation of six acres to the Leon River marked the beginning of Texas' first state park. Her son, Pat Neff, significantly augmented this by contributing an additional 250 acres. Developed by the Civilian Conservation Corps, the park faced challenges from flooding, necessitating ongoing repairs. Today, Mother Neff State Park is a shining example of familial generosity and commitment to preservation. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
